intro.text: The ruling council of Luthadel, created by King Elend Venture as part of the government he built after the Lord Ruler's fall.

description.text: It has twenty-four members, eight each from the nobility, the skaa workers and the merchants, a mix Elend chose so commoners could outvote nobles, though the merchants hold themselves aloof from, and superior to, other skaa. The king presides and breaks ties; with no king, a chancellor chosen by majority does it.
Elend meant it to advise the king and voice the people's concerns, but also gave it real power, so it could stop a king becoming a tyrant.
A two-thirds vote lets it suspend its own authority so the city can be surrendered, and a unanimous one can expel a member. It also rules on everyday matters, such as who controls the food stores.

It can depose the king by a unanimous vote of all but the king. It then has a month to elect a new one by a two-thirds majority from nominees, who may include the deposed king; if it fails, he returns and cannot be removed for a year.

items.text: After the Lord Ruler's death, Elend talked the rioting skaa into building a new government on democratic lines. Named king, he led the drafting of a constitution and created the Assembly so the people could share power and the king could be advised and checked. It met in the old Canton of Finance building.
With Straff Venture's army outside, Elend persuades the Assembly, by the two-thirds it needs, not to vote on the city's fate until he has tried talking to his father.

Worried by the coming winter, scarce food and fuel, and a small, mostly untrained army, the Assembly leans toward handing the city to Straff. A second army, under Ashweather Cett, makes it more nervous still.
While Elend is away at his father's camp, the Assembly holds a vote of no confidence and removes him as king.
The law that let it unseat him is one Elend wrote himself. Though his friends press him to declare martial law, he refuses and looks for a lawful way back to the throne.
Elend has Lord Ferson Penrod made chancellor to lead the Assembly while there is no king. Penrod, Elend and Cett are then put forward for the throne.
Cett comes before the Assembly to argue that he should be king, offering rewards to those who vote for him.

On election day Elend declares himself a follower of the Survivor to win skaa votes, but assassins attack the hall. The Assembly meets again at Penrod's mansion, and after two members change their votes, Penrod is elected king by a two-thirds majority.
Straff had bought Assembly votes for Penrod, and in return for his support Penrod agrees to hand the city over to him.
After the battle with Straff's army, Vin compels Penrod, Cett and Janarle to take Elend as their emperor.
Penrod keeps his throne under Elend, and the Assembly keeps its powers, subject to an imperial veto. Elend also uses it as a model for councils in the other cities he brings into his empire.
